hz2_invasion.topic: Operation Peace for Galilee, the siege of Beirut, Sabra and Shatila, 1982

claims.text: Shlomo Argov, Israel's ambassador in London, was shot and severely injured on 3 June 1982 by a militant of the Abu Nidal Organization; the attempt led to Operation Peace for Galilee; he died of his injuries in 2003
Arutz Sheva (2003): Israeli jets bombed PLO depots and bases the day after the shooting; the PLO shelled northern Israel; the IDF launched the operation on 6 June

IDF official account: operation launched 6 June 1982 'following the attempted assassination of the Israeli Ambassador to the UK'; objective 'pushing the latter 40 km to the north'; war lasted more than three months; siege of Beirut hardened from late June; evacuation by sea under an international force completed 31 August

Begin Heritage Center: operation 'designed to harm terror organizations and ensure that the forty miles surrounding the border would be terrorist-free'; IDF 'was forced to continue north all the way to Beirut'; Arafat forced to leave in August; IDF later withdrew to the security zone
9 June 1982: Israeli Air Force destroyed 17 of 19 Syrian SAM batteries in the Bekaa (Mole Cricket 19); 13 June IDF reached West Beirut
MNF of US, French and Italian troops arrived in Beirut 24 August 1982 to oversee the PLO withdrawal
Marines withdrew 10 September 1982 after the PLO left; redeployed 29 September 1982 after the Sabra and Shatila massacre (16-18 September); the invasion had tacit US approval

Sabra and Shatila: Kataeb (Phalange) members killed between 762 and 3,500 civilians, mostly Palestinians and Lebanese Shia, in camps Israeli troops had surrounded; presented as retaliation for the assassination of president-elect Bachir Gemayel; 400,000 marched in Israel on 25 September 1982 demanding Begin's resignation
NJOP gives 656 Israelis killed in action and 3,887 wounded (window not stated) and stated aim 'pushing the PLO 40 KM further north'
